question: In *Meenakshi Natarajan v. ECI* (June 2026), the Supreme Court held that:

options.text: Article 32 writs can stay an election if "glaring" illegality is shown
Article 329(b) bars judicial interference once an election process has begun; the only remedy is an election petition after the poll
The Election Commission alone can adjudicate nomination disputes
Rajya Sabha by-elections are outside the scope of Article 329(b)

explanation: The Court held Article 329(b) bars writ interference once an election process has begun, with no exception even for "glaring" illegality; the only remedy is a post-poll election petition.
